content.text:
I've built and pushed Haq in four commits, but none of the Claude-powered parts have actually run yet. There's no `.env`, so I have no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`.

**To continue:** create `.env` from `.env.example`, fill in both keys, and tell me when it's done. I won't print or commit them. I'll then do one interview plus a full run on one household, run the evals (first on a couple of households, then all 20), commit the results file and fix whatever breaks.

**What I've tested so far:**
- The server starts, serves the page and creates a household.
- The page fetcher works against real government sites. It recovered from a simulated failure, retried an expired certificate on sspy-up.gov.in, and moved from pmjay.gov.in (timed out) to another official page.
- The eval scoring works on made-up predictions.

**What's built:**
- **App** (`app.py`, `static/index.html`): a big Hindi mic button with a text box fallback. Questions and answers are spoken aloud in Hindi. Results are large cards with an emoji, the ₹ per year, which family member, documents needed, where to apply and an official source link, under a headline total.
  - A family that comes back sees its saved results and can ask follow-up questions.
  - Any search that was interrupted resumes when the server restarts.
- **Agent** (`haq/agent.py`): a short Hindi interview (it never asks about caste), then a plan of candidate schemes per member. Each scheme then gets its own research loop using web search and an official-page fetch tool.
  - The code rejects a scheme unless every eligibility rule cites an official page the agent actually read. Unverifiable schemes are dropped, and disagreements with unofficial sites are logged with a reason.
- **Recovery** (`haq/fetcher.py`): each page is tried 3 times with increasing waits, then the scheme's other official pages are tried. `SIMULATE_FAILURE=1` makes the first lookup fail for the demo.
- **State**: everything is saved to `data/state.json` after every step, so families can return and a crashed run picks up where it stopped.
- **Tracing**: every Claude call, agent step and tool call is traced in neatlogs, grouped by household.
- **Evals**:
  - `evals/families.json` has 20 UP households and 55 expected schemes, each with an official source URL and `needs_human_check: true`. It includes negative cases, such as a farmer who pays income tax being excluded from PM-KISAN and a divorced mother not getting the widow pension.
  - `run_evals.py` reports precision, recall, accuracy, average cost and average time, and saves `evals/results-<timestamp>.json` with the change from the previous run.

**Please check:**
- **Eval answers:** several state portals only load content with JavaScript or had broken pages, so some rules and amounts are from my own knowledge plus the portal home pages. Two to spot-check first:
  - the income limits for the UP pensions
  - whether the UP pension limits rule out the joint family in household h12 (I marked that pension optional)
- **Insecure retry:** when a government site's security certificate has expired, the fetcher retries once without checking it. It only reads public pages and logs that it did this.
- **Insurance schemes don't count either way in scoring:** insurance and contributory products (PMJJBY, PMSBY, PM-SYM, e-Shram, crop insurance) are marked "acceptable extra". Haq isn't penalised for finding or missing them. The README explains this.
- **Fallback setting:** I turned on Anthropic's refusal fallback, which retries a declined request on another model within the same call. It's easy to turn off if you don't want it.
- **Model and cost:** Haq uses Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort. I'll report real cost per household after the first live run. You can switch models with `HAQ_MODEL`.
- **Python version:** neatlogs needs Python below 3.14, so I made a Python 3.12 environment in `.venv`.

I don't have an eval score yet: the Anthropic account ran out of credit partway through the first test household. Neither the test household nor the full evals have finished.

**Sonnet default:** done and pushed. `claude-sonnet-5-5` is now the default for the app and the evals; you can switch back with `HAQ_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5`.

**Test household.** I read your description as a three-generation family, since the mother can't be a widow while the father is alive: the farmer's widowed mother (62), the farmer (40, owns 2 acres), his wife, a daughter (13) and a son (10), rural Sitapur. If you meant something else, tell me. I ran it with `SIMULATE_FAILURE=1`. Haq planned 14 candidate schemes and finished 10 before the credit error:

| Result | Scheme | Official source it confirmed on |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ verified | PM-KISAN (father), ₹6,000/yr | pmkisan.gov.in |
| ✅ verified | Widow pension (mother), ₹12,000/yr | sspy-up.gov.in |
| ✅ verified | Ration card (NFSA) | nfsa.gov.in |
| ✅ verified | PM Kisan Maandhan, PMSBY, Shadi Anudan | pmkmy.gov.in, pib.gov.in, shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in |
| ❌ dropped | Old-age pension (mother) | Family income is over the UP limit on the official samajkalyan page |
| ❌ dropped | Kanya Sumangala (daughter) | No benefit stage applies to a class 8 girl right now |
| ❌ dropped | PMAY-G, crop insurance | The official pages only load with JavaScript, so it couldn't confirm the rules |

- **Recovery works:** the simulated failure on pmkisan.gov.in was retried with backoff and then succeeded. The JavaScript-only myscheme page fell back to another official URL.
- **Resume bug, now fixed:** schemes that hit the credit error were being saved as "dropped", so resuming would have skipped them. They now stay unfinished and the run is marked failed, so resuming retries them. I removed the 4 wrong records from this test run and pushed the fix.
- **Not yet tested:** the final card-writing and summary step never ran, because that's where the credit ran out.
- **Accuracy issue:** PMAY-G being dropped for a rural kutcha house is a likely recall loss in the evals. The eval run will show how often this happens.

**Cost:** $0.88 for 10 schemes, so about $1.20 per household and roughly **$25 for all 20 evals** on Sonnet.

**neatlogs:** the SDK reports traces were sent successfully: flush returned true and there were 0 export failures. The SDK can't confirm from the server side, so please check the dashboard for workflow `haq`. You should see a `haq_run` trace with `plan`, the `research:<scheme>` agent spans, the LLM spans inside them, and the `fetch_official_page` tool spans including the failed attempt. They're grouped by session `1039c7bd51`.

**To finish:** add about $30 of credit at console.anthropic.com → Plans & Billing and tell me when it's done. I'll resume this household (only the 4 remaining schemes plus the write step get re-run), then run all 20 evals and report precision, recall, accuracy, cost and time.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
The first 10 households (h01–h10) scored **precision 0.72, recall 0.66, accuracy 0.51**, at an average of **$0.92 and 142 seconds per household**. All 10 completed without errors. The results file is pushed as `evals/results-20261010-160806.json`.

**First household cost:** $1.12 in total. $0.88 was spent before the credit ran out and $0.24 on the resume, which re-ran only the 4 unfinished schemes plus the write step. Most of the cost is cache writes from the web-search context in each research loop. My estimate for all 20 households is **$18–22**; the measured $0.92 average puts it at about $18.50.

**Results on h01–h10 (Sonnet 5.5):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Precision | **0.72** |
| Recall | **0.66** |
| F1 | 0.69 |
| Accuracy (TP / (TP + FP + FN)) | **0.51** |
| Avg cost per household | **$0.92** (total $9.23) |
| Avg time per household | **142 s** (4 households in parallel) |
| Recoveries / conflicts logged | 253 / 0 |

**Why it misses schemes (11 missed):** in every case Haq planned the scheme, but no official page it could read stated the rules, so it dropped the scheme as unverifiable.
- **UP scholarship, 4 misses:** scholarship.up.gov.in never loaded. The fallback was the national scholarship portal's home page, which has no UP rules, and the income limits only appeared on non-government sites like buddy4study.
- **PMAY-G (rural housing), 2 misses:** pmayg.dord.gov.in only returns its home page, without eligibility rules.
- **Ration card for families that don't have one, 2 misses:** nfsa.gov.in says each state sets the rules, and Haq couldn't open the UP food department's rules page.
- **Widow pension, PM-JAY and the construction-worker board (BOCW), 1 miss each:** the official pages didn't load or didn't show the full rules. The widow pension page confirmed "widow, 18+", but Haq wanted the income limit too and dropped it.

**Why it gets wrong schemes (8 wrong):**
- **Ration card, 6 cases:** Haq recommended it to families that already hold one. The profile records the card, but Haq doesn't treat it as "already receiving".
- **Shadi Anudan (marriage grant), 2 cases:** recommended for young daughters. It's a one-time grant at marriage and these families are over the income limit. This is the same error as in your test household.

**Fixes I'd make next**, likely to raise both precision and recall:
1. Treat an existing ration card as already received.
2. Only suggest Shadi Anudan when a marriage is actually coming up.
3. Accept the core rule confirmed on an official page (e.g. "widow, 18+") and note the unconfirmed income limit as an assumption, instead of dropping the scheme.
4. Add official PDF and rules pages that do load, such as the scholarship and PMAY-G guidelines, to the list of fallback sources.

"0 conflicts logged" suggests the agent isn't calling the conflict log even when it reads non-government sites. I'll check that too.

**neatlogs:** the SDK reported 0 export failures on the test household. The eval traces are under the workflow `haq-evals`, with one `eval:h01` … `eval:h10` trace each. Please confirm they appear in the dashboard; I can't see it from here.

Should I make these fixes and re-run the same 10 households (about $9) to get the before/after comparison, or run h11–h20 first on the current code (about $9)?

     on (including any income limit) on an official page.

     9-10") and the member clearly meets it, but the ONLY rule you could not find on an official page is the
     income limit / poverty-line criterion. List that in unconfirmed_rules. The family will be told
     "Likely eligible - confirm income limit". If the member's income is clearly above a limit you did confirm,
     drop instead.
   - drop_scheme: the member does not qualify, or you could not confirm the core eligibility on any official page.

""")
rep('''        "description": "Final answer: the member is eligible and the rules were confirmed on an official page.",''',

rep('''            "required": ["scheme_id", "scheme_name_hi", "member", "official_url", "rules_checked",

''','''                "official_url": {"type": "string", "description": "official page where the rules were confirmed"},
                "verification": {"type": "string", "enum": ["confirmed", "likely"]},
                "unconfirmed_rules": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"},
                                      "description": "empty for confirmed; for likely, the income-limit rule(s) not found officially"},
''')

                return ("REJECTED: verification=likely needs unconfirmed_rules naming the income-limit rule you "
                        "could not confirm. If everything is confirmed, use verification=confirmed."), True, None
            if args["verification"] == "confirmed":

            status = "verified" if args["verification"] == "confirmed" else "likely"

        total = sum(c["annual_value_inr"] for c in cards if c["counts_toward_total"])
        brief = [{"name": c["name_hi"], "member": c["member"], "benefit": c["benefit_hi"],
                  "value": c["annual_value_inr"], "counted": c["counts_toward_total"]} for c in cards]''','''        cards.sort(key=lambda c: (c["verification"] != "confirmed", -int(c["counts_toward_total"]),
                                  -c["annual_value_inr"]))
        total = sum(c["annual_value_inr"] for c in cards if c["counts_toward_total"])
        likely_total = sum(c["annual_value_inr"] for c in cards if c["counts_toward_likely_total"])
        brief = [{"name": c["name_hi"], "member": c["member"], "benefit": c["benefit_hi"],

SUMMARY_SCHEMA = {''')

content.thinking: I found the real culprit: my error-handling code cancels futures on credit errors, but since `CancelledError` is a `BaseException` in Python 3.8+, it slips past `except Exception` and leaves the run hanging on executor threads—plus the Anthropic client's 10-minute timeout with 4 retries can stall up to 50 minutes, and fetches lack a total deadline. I'll fix all three issues now.

content.content:
9:The cache key is derived from the exact bytes of the rendered prompt up to each `cache_control` breakpoint. A single byte difference at position N - a timestamp, a reordered JSON key, a different tool in the list - invalidates the cache for all breakpoints at positions >= N.
11:Render order is: `tools` -> `system` -> `messages`. A breakpoint on the last system block caches both tools and system together.
23:   - Never changes -> belongs early in the prompt, before any breakpoint
25:   - Changes per-turn -> belongs at the end, after the last breakpoint
28:4. **Place breakpoints at stability boundaries.** See placement patterns below.
37:Put a breakpoint on the last system text block. If there are tools, they render before system - the marker on the last system block caches tools + system together.
47:Put a breakpoint on the last content block of the most-recently-appended turn. Each subsequent request reuses the entire prior conversation prefix. Earlier breakpoints remain valid read points, so hits accrue incrementally as the conversation grows.
56:Many requests share a large fixed preamble (few-shot examples, retrieved docs, instructions) but differ in the final question. Put the breakpoint at the end of the **shared** portion, not at the end of the whole prompt - otherwise every request writes a distinct cache entry and nothing is ever read.
67:**Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and Claude Sonnet 5.5; no beta header. Not available on Claude Sonnet 5** - use top-level `system` there. (Sources conflict on Claude Sonnet 5: the model config marks it supported, but every canonical docs page omits it. Treat it as unsupported and catch the 400.) When an operator instruction arrives mid-conversation - a mode switch, updated context, dynamically injected state - send it as `{"role": "system", "content": "..."}` appended to `messages[]`, rather than editing top-level `system`. Editing top-level `system` changes the prefix ahead of the entire conversation history, so every cached turn is re-processed uncached; a `role: "system"` message sits after the history and leaves the cached prefix intact.
70:// Top-level system stays byte-identical; new instruction goes after the cached history
81:Must follow a `role: "user"` message (or an `assistant` message ending in server-tool use), and must be either the last entry in `messages` or be followed by an `assistant` turn; cannot be `messages[0]` - use top-level `system` for the initial prompt. Content is text-only. Unsupported models return a 400 (`BadRequestError`: `role 'system' is not supported on this model`); catch that error and fall back to putting the instruction in a user-turn `<system-reminder>` block.
83:**Per-turn reminders in a tool loop: turn-scoped messages, never deleted.** A reminder injected into history and removed on the next request is a history edit - the cache misses from that point and, on Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5, every later thinking block is invalidated. Instead give the `role: "system"` message `clear_at: "next_user_message"` (beta `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`; same models and platforms as mid-conversation system messages): it renders for one turn, then stays in the transcript cleared - costing no input tokens, not cache-eligible (`cache_control` on it is a 400; put the breakpoint on the preceding user turn), and still part of the prefix. Append a fresh copy after each `tool_result` message and leave earlier copies in place; without the beta, a `text` block after the `tool_result` blocks in the same user message, earlier copies kept. Separately, per-message effort (beta `mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01`; Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5 with thinking on; Claude API and Google Cloud): a `role: "system"` message with `content: []` and `output_config: {effort: ...}` changes effort from the next user turn on **without** the messages-cache invalidation that a top-level `effort` change causes, and is exempt from the placement rules (it can sit anywhere) - see the Invalidation hierarchy below and `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 from Claude Fable 5 -> New API features.

def _research_wave(wave, profile, usage, hid, rid, abort, errors):
    """Research candidates in parallel; save each finished record as soon as it completes."""
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(RESEARCH_WORKERS) as pool:
                futs = {pool.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, research_one, profile, c, usage, hid, rid,
                                    abort): c
                        for c in wave}
                for fut in as_completed(futs):
                    c = futs[fut]
                    try:
                        rec = fut.result()
                    except Exception as e:
                        # Not saved: the candidate stays unfinished so a resume retries it.
                        errors.append(f"{c['key']}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300])
                        if isinstance(e, (anthropic.AuthenticationError, anthropic.PermissionDeniedError,
                                          anthropic.BadRequestError)):
                            abort.set()  # the same error will hit every call; other loops stop at their next turn
                        continue

                    def _save(r, c=c, rec=rec):
                        r["research"][c["key"]] = rec
                        r["conflicts"].extend({**x, "scheme": c["key"]} for x in rec.get("conflicts", []))
                        r["recovery_log"].extend({**x, "scheme": c["key"]} for x in rec.get("recovery_log", []))
                        r.setdefault("unofficial_claims", []).extend(
                            {**x, "scheme": c["key"]} for x in rec.get("unofficial_claims", []))
                        r["usage"] = usage.snapshot()
                    state.update_run(hid, rid, _save)

content.text:
I've made all four cost changes as separate commits, but by my estimate they make Haq about 4x cheaper, not 10x. Re-running the households that went wrong would cost about **$2.10** (likely range $1.40–2.90), versus $8.35 for the same households in the baseline. I made no evals or live calls; everything was tested offline with a stub client.

**Commits:**

| Commit | Change | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| `Cost: cache official pages and verified scheme rules on disk` | Official pages are kept 7 days and a scheme's verified rules 30 days. Rules are per scheme, with no family data. Haq checks each scheme once and serves the other family members from the cache. | The baseline made 121 lookups for only 24 distinct schemes; PMSBY alone was looked up 19 times. |
| `Cost: Haiku for interview/plan/summary/follow-ups, Sonnet only for verification` | Model chosen per task, configurable in `.env`. The refusal fallback is only sent to Sonnet, because Haiku doesn't support it. | Simple steps were running on Sonnet. |
| `Cost: max 2 web searches per scheme; stop as soon as an official page confirms` | Searches are counted per scheme: after 2 Sonnet is told to stop, and a 3rd ends that scheme. No web search at all when rules are cached. Max 6 turns. | Web searches and their re-cached results were most of the baseline cost. |
| `Cost: prompt caching for the system prompt and scheme rules` | The shared instructions are cached once for all schemes, and each scheme's rules once for every family. Short one-off steps only cache their instructions. | Nothing was shared between lookups before. |

I filled the rules cache offline from the baseline's verified results, so 19 schemes are cached without paying for those lookups again.

**Which households to re-run:** no household actually crashed in the baseline. I'm reading "had errors" as households with a wrong or missed scheme, which is **9 of the 10: h01–h07, h09 and h10**. Only h08 was fully correct.

**Estimate for those 9 households:**
- Today's planner fixes remove 10 of their 109 lookups, leaving 99.
- 94 of those 99 have cached rules, so they need no web search. Each is about one Sonnet turn at roughly $0.012–0.025.
- 5 still need web research: UP scholarship, NSP, BOCW, Abhyudaya and DigiShakti. Each costs about $0.06–0.11, and the first lookup caches the rules for the rest.
- Haiku for planning and the summary adds under $0.01 per household.

| | Baseline | Estimate after changes |
|---|---|---|
| Total for 9 households | $8.35 | **~$2.10** ($1.40–2.90) |
| Per household | $0.93 | ~$0.23 ($0.16–0.33) |
| Cheaper by | | ~4x (3–6x) |

**Why it's not 10x:** almost all the remaining cost is Sonnet's written answer on the 94 cached lookups. Two more changes would get close to 10x. Tell me if you want them:
1. Verify all members for the same scheme in one Sonnet call. For example, PMSBY for 3 members becomes one call instead of three.
2. Use lower Sonnet effort when cached rules already exist.

**Caveats:**
- **Untested against the live API:** Haiku with structured outputs, and the new prompt-cache layout. If the cache layout doesn't work as designed, the cost rises toward the high end of the range, but it won't fail.
- **Haiku cache prices are my assumption:** I used the usual 0.1x read / 1.25x write of input, because only Haiku's input/output prices were listed.
- **Cached rules come from the baseline's own lookups:** they were confirmed on official pages, but they inherit any gaps, such as a missing income limit. Sonnet is told to check the official page, or mark the scheme "Likely eligible", when a rule it needs isn't in the cache.
- **Re-runs reuse the cache:** for a cold-cache run, set `HAQ_NO_CACHE=1` (cost goes back to roughly $0.90 per household).

I won't run anything until you say so.

I couldn't run the smoke test: the API account has no credit left. The very first request, a one-line Haiku interview turn, came back with "credit balance is too low". Nothing ran and nothing was charged, and I stopped there.

Both changes you approved are committed and pushed as separate commits. All checks so far were offline with a fake model, so everything that needs the real API is still unconfirmed:
- Haiku structured outputs
- prompt-cache reads
- the actual cost per household

**Commits since your last message:**

| Commit | Change | Checked offline |
|---|---|---|
| `Cost: one research loop per scheme, deciding all of a family's members together` | One loop per scheme decides every member at once, e.g. PMSBY for the father, mother and son in one turn instead of three loops. Member names are matched regardless of case; unknown names are rejected and a member left undecided is dropped with a reason. | A 3-member scheme decided correctly, including an unknown name and a lowercase "wife" |
| `Cost: low Sonnet effort when only applying fully confirmed cached rules` | Effort is "low" only when the cached rules are fully confirmed. It stays "medium" for real research or when an income limit is still unconfirmed. | Confirmed cache → low, likely-only cache → medium, no cache → medium |
| `Report usage and cost per model (calls, tokens, cache reads/writes)` | Saves Haiku and Sonnet usage separately, so the smoke test can show Haiku doing planning and the summary, and the cache reads on each model. | Breakdown adds up and survives resume |

**Updated estimate for the 9 baseline households with a wrong or missed scheme:** about **$1.00–1.60 in total, or $0.11–0.18 per household**, against $0.93 in the baseline. That's roughly 5–8x cheaper. The new saving comes from merging same-scheme lookups for different members within a family, about 99 lookups down to about 70 scheme loops, and from low effort on most of them. This is still an estimate until a live run.

**Once there's credit, the plan is the same as you set:**
1. Smoke test on **h09** (the 74-year-old widow, which the baseline got wrong), plus one Haiku interview turn. I'll report actual cost, the per-model breakdown, and the cache reads that confirm prompt caching.
2. If h09 costs under $0.30, run the other 8 (h01–h07, h10) at the baseline's settings (4 households in parallel) so the times are comparable. Then the final table: baseline vs after for accuracy, precision, recall, wrong and missed schemes, cost per household in USD and ₹, and time. Likely-eligible schemes will be reported separately from confirmed ones.
3. Last, a cold-cache run (`HAQ_NO_CACHE=1`) of h09 alone, for the warm vs cold cost comparison.

Total needed is about **$2–3**: roughly $0.15 for h09, $1.00–1.40 for the other 8, and $0.40–0.80 for the cold run. If the credit can't be topped up, steps 1 and 2 need only about $1.50.

content.text:
On the 9 households that had a wrong or missed scheme in the baseline, Haq now costs **about 4x less per household ($0.93 → $0.22)** and gets **accuracy from 0.50 to 0.86**. Half of those right answers are "likely eligible" rather than confirmed. h09 alone came in at $0.112, under your $0.30 limit, so I ran the other 8 and then a cold-cache run of h09. The result files are committed and pushed.

**Smoke test confirmations (h09):**
- **Haiku structured outputs work.** A test interview turn returned a valid profile, and the plan and summary steps returned valid structured output.
- **Prompt caching works on both models.** Sonnet read 5,656 tokens from cache in the warm run. In the cold run, Haiku's plan step read 2,646 cached tokens left by the warm run a few minutes earlier.

**Baseline vs after (the same 9 households):**

| | Baseline | After |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.50 | **0.86** |
| Precision | 0.71 | **0.97** |
| Recall | 0.64 | **0.89** |
| Wrong schemes | 8 | **1** |
| Missed schemes | 10 | **3** |
| Cost per household | $0.93 (≈ ₹82) | **$0.22 (≈ ₹20)** |
| Total for 9 households | $8.35 (≈ ₹735) | **$2.00 (≈ ₹176)** |
| Time per household | 147 s | **59 s** |

- **Rupee conversion:** I assumed ₹88 per US dollar; I didn't look up a live rate.
- **Time comparison:** the 8 households ran 4 at a time, like the baseline. h09 ran alone, which flatters the after time slightly.

**Likely-eligible vs confirmed:**
- **15 of the 28 matches are "Likely eligible — confirm income limit".** 13 of those were expected answers, 2 were optional extras, and none were wrong.
- **Counting only confirmed schemes:** precision is 0.94 but recall drops to **0.54** (accuracy 0.52).
- **What's in the likely group:** mostly the widow and old-age pensions, PM-JAY, UP scholarships and the ration card. For these the official pages confirm who qualifies, but not the income limit.

**Warm vs cold cache (h09, same household):**

| | Cost | Time | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm cache | $0.112 (≈ ₹10) | 47 s | 4/4, 0 wrong |
| Cold cache (`HAQ_NO_CACHE=1`) | $0.241 (≈ ₹21) | 122 s | 4/4, 0 wrong |

A cold run is still about 4x cheaper than the baseline. The warm cache had rules for 19 schemes, imported from the baseline runs that were already paid for.

**What's still wrong (4 errors):**
- h05 got PM Vishwakarma for a construction worker. That's arguably defensible, since masons are one of its trades, but it isn't in the expected list.
- h05 missed the UP construction-workers board scheme (BOCW) and Ujjwala.
- h06 missed Kanya Sumangala.

I didn't change any expected answers.

**Other things to know:**
- **Conflict log:** across the 8 households, 8 claims found only on non-government sites were logged and not used as rules. There were 0 direct conflicts, because Sonnet mostly worked from cached official rules and searched less.
- **Spend:** this session spent about $2.24 in total. 10 households (h08 and h11–h20) haven't been run on the new code. At about $0.22 each, that would be roughly $2.20.

# Evidence: Haq before vs after

This file shows what changed between the first eval run (the baseline) and the current code, and the evidence
behind each change. Every number below comes from the committed results files in `evals/`. No expected answer in
`evals/families.json` has been changed since it was created in
[`893473d`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/893473de9dda7fca0b87d8f9e44382bc841218c2).

| Run | Results file | Households | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Baseline** | `evals/results-20261010-160806.json` | h01–h10 | Sonnet 5.5 for every step, no cache, 4 workers |
| After: smoke test, warm cache | `evals/results-20261010-171541.json` | h09 | current code, 1 worker |
| After: warm cache | `evals/results-20261010-171810.json` | h01–h07, h10 | current code, 4 workers |
| After: cold cache | `evals/results-20261010-172025.json` | h09 | current code, `HAQ_NO_CACHE=1`, 1 worker |

## 1. Before vs after

These are the **9 households that had a wrong or missed scheme in the baseline**: h01–h07, h09 and h10. h08 was
fully correct in the baseline and was not re-run. The "after" column uses the warm-cache h09 run and the batch of
8. Rupee amounts use an assumed rate of ₹88 per US dollar.

| Metric | Baseline | After |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy (TP / (TP + FP + FN)) | 0.50 | **0.86** |
| Precision | 0.71 | **0.97** |
| Recall | 0.64 | **0.89** |
| Wrong schemes (FP) | 8 | **1** |
| Missed schemes (FN) | 10 | **3** |
| Cost per household | $0.93 (≈ ₹82) | **$0.22 (≈ ₹20)** |
| Total cost for 9 households | $8.35 (≈ ₹735) | **$2.00 (≈ ₹176)** |
| Time per household | 147 s | **59 s** |

Per household:

| Household | Baseline: wrong / missed | After: wrong / missed | After: cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| h01 | nfsa_ration, up_shadi_anudan / up_scholarship | — / — | $0.270 |
| h02 | up_shadi_anudan / up_widow_pension, pmjay, pmay_g | — / — | $0.239 |
| h03 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.073 |
| h04 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.185 |
| h05 | — / up_bocw, nfsa_ration | pm_vishwakarma / up_bocw, pmuy | $0.205 |
| h06 | nfsa_ration / up_scholarship | — / up_kanya_sumangala | $0.337 |
| h07 | — / nfsa_ration, pmay_g | — / — | $0.353 |
| h09 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.112 |
| h10 | nfsa_ration / up_scholarship | — / — | $0.226 |

Known remaining errors:

- **h05, wrong scheme:** PM Vishwakarma for a construction worker. This is arguably defensible, because masons
  are one of the scheme's trades, but it is not in the expected list.
- **h05, missed schemes:** UP BOCW and Ujjwala.
- **h06, missed scheme:** Kanya Sumangala.

## 2. Likely eligible vs confirmed

A scheme is labelled **"Likely eligible — confirm income limit"** when its core eligibility (who the scheme is
for) is confirmed on an official page but the income limit is not. Likely schemes are shown on the cards with that
label and are not counted in the confirmed ₹ total.

| Group | Number of predictions | Expected answer | Optional extra | Wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Likely eligible | 15 | 13 | 2 | **0** |
| Confirmed | 15 | 15 | — | 1 (h05 PM Vishwakarma) |

| Metric (same 9 households) | All predictions | Confirmed only |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.86 | 0.52 |
| Precision | 0.97 | 0.94 |
| Recall | 0.89 | 0.54 |

The likely group is mostly the widow and old-age pensions, PM-JAY, UP scholarships and the ration card. For these
schemes the official portals confirm who qualifies but do not publish the income limit.

## 3. Warm vs cold cache (h09, same household)

| | Warm cache | Cold cache (`HAQ_NO_CACHE=1`) |
|---|---|---|
| Cost | **$0.112** (≈ ₹10) | $0.241 (≈ ₹21) |
| Time | 47 s | 122 s |
| Score | 4/4, 0 wrong | 4/4, 0 wrong |
| Sonnet calls / cost | 6 / $0.111 | 14 / $0.240 |
| Haiku calls / cost | 2 / $0.001 | 2 / $0.001 |
| Web searches | 0 | 3 |
| Sonnet tokens read from cache / written to cache | 5,656 / 18,018 | 200,637 / 27,646 |

What this shows:

- **Haiku structured outputs work.** The interview, plan and summary steps all returned valid structured output.
- **Prompt caching works on both models.** In the cold run, the Haiku plan step read 2,646 cached tokens that the
  warm run had written a few minutes earlier.
- **Where the warm-cache rules came from.** The warm cache holds rules for 19 schemes. They were imported, with no
  new API calls, from baseline lookups that had already been paid for (`python -m haq.cache seed`).

## 4. Fixes, commits and the evidence for each

### About the neatlogs trace identifiers

The **neatlogs trace IDs (OpenTelemetry trace ids) were not recorded at run time**, so they are not listed here.
Each bug below is identified instead by three things, which together are enough to find the trace in the neatlogs
dashboard:

- the **trace name**, for example `eval:h03`, in workflow `haq-evals`
- the **span name**, for example `research:nfsa_ration:household`
- the **session id**, which is the household id

| Run | Session ids (household ids) |
|---|---|
| Baseline | h01 `1d89d89faa`, h02 `f7de572297`, h03 `eee3110444`, h04 `531b815edb`, h05 `656e07dcc6`, h06 `819b1ae51c`, h07 `cf70fbe6c8`, h08 `b45c4ae89e`, h09 `f4980ec823`, h10 `391532689f` |
| Aborted re-run, before fixes 6–7 | h01 `b0a76752da`, h02 `0dc8661720`, h03 `9621321743`, h04 `0a706b5470` |
| Manual test household (workflow `haq`) | `1039c7bd51` |

### Accuracy fixes

| # | Fix | Commit | Evidence (neatlogs trace / span / session) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Don't recommend a ration card to families that already hold one | [`658fe54`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/658fe5471f83970aa72a3b5b973c04fdf76a834d) | `eval:h01`, `eval:h03`, `eval:h04`, `eval:h06`, `eval:h09`, `eval:h10`. Span `research:nfsa_ration:household` ended in `record_verified` even though the profile already had an Antyodaya or eligible-household card. This caused 6 of the 8 baseline wrong schemes. Sessions are the baseline ids above. |
| 2 | Marriage grants only when a marriage is actually coming up | [`bddd5d9`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/bddd5d9921cba320f156cc74ee776b920680f192) | `eval:h01` (`1d89d89faa`) and `eval:h02` (`f7de572297`). Span `research:up_shadi_anudan:daughter` recorded the scheme for girls aged 12 and 7. The same bug appeared in the manual test `1039c7bd51` (daughter aged 13). |
| 3 | "Likely eligible — confirm income limit" instead of dropping the scheme | [`5baa497`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/5baa497f20a3adc52b65900e1652a09dd7dc32c8) | `eval:h02` (`f7de572297`): `research:up_widow_pension:self` was dropped although sspy-up.gov.in confirmed "widow, 18+". `eval:h06` (`819b1ae51c`) and `eval:h10` (`391532689f`): `research:up_scholarship:*` was dropped because the income limit appeared only on buddy4study. |
| 4 | Read official rule PDFs and the legacy-TLS state portals | [`30fbc1f`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/30fbc1f7bf0e83dd8c521ac5fcf156f2a8d269b8) | `eval:h01`, `eval:h06`, `eval:h10`: the `fetch_url_with_retry` spans for scholarship.up.gov.in failed 3 out of 3 times with `SSL: UNSAFE_LEGACY_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED`. This caused all 4 scholarship misses. `eval:h02` and `eval:h07` (`cf70fbe6c8`): `research:pmay_g:household` found only the portal home page, while the rules are in the guidelines PDF. |
| 5 | Actually record conflicts when non-government sources are read | [`6b33c05`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/6b33c05af8d6d35f64e17f402a3ad8ea04f5348e) | The baseline logged 0 conflicts. Meanwhile `eval:h06` relied on buddy4study, `eval:h07` on kotak811 and bajajfinserv, and `eval:h02` on private sites for PM-JAY. After the fix, 8 unofficial claims were logged and none were used as a rule. |
| 6 | Tolerate stringified tool arrays; stop hung runs after a fatal API error | [`d0acca4`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/d0acca40ac86b96d7c25d1007c7f71a4f66d64c9) | Aborted re-run, `eval:h03` (`9621321743`): `research:ayushman_vay_vandana:self` raised `TypeError: string indices must be integers`. Aborted re-run, `eval:h01`, `eval:h02`, `eval:h04` (`b0a76752da`, `0dc8661720`, `0a706b5470`): runs stayed `running` for 30+ minutes because a `CancelledError` escaped `except Exception`. This commit contains both fixes. |
| 7 | Bound every network wait (API client timeout, fetch deadline) | [`c4f4f2e`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/c4f4f2efe12f8f55bee38c4567039ff63370fefb) | Same aborted re-run, `eval:h01`, `eval:h02`, `eval:h04`: research spans stayed open for 30+ minutes. Neither the API client nor page downloads had a total time limit. |
| — | Don't save failed lookups, so a resume retries them | [`4e86960`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/4e8696050afa474788a837f47544d44ecc9eb524) | Manual test `1039c7bd51` (workflow `haq`): 4 candidates were saved as "dropped" with a billing error as the reason. |

### Cost fixes

The evidence for these is the baseline token profile (results file `20261010-160806`):

- **$4.92 of the $9.23 (53%) was cache writes** of web-search results.
- There were **121 scheme lookups for only 24 distinct schemes**. PMSBY was looked up 19 times and PMJJBY 15 times.

| # | Change | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Cache official pages (7 days) and verified scheme rules (30 days) on disk | [`0138493`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/0138493ca10acfad6e25333ff5a3d0a2b8f7c890) |
| C2 | Haiku for the interview, plan, summary and follow-ups; Sonnet only for verification | [`9c0ecf2`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/9c0ecf27199f6ab612c30a63abec34cf2e266546) |
| C3 | At most 2 web searches per scheme; stop once an official page confirms the rules | [`52498bf`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/52498bf2c082d0d33ffe16b44204eec4a857ae48) |
| C4 | Prompt caching for the system prompt and scheme rules | [`bc74be2`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/bc74be23cffc31f93b9873cf07f86de6c98677ae) |
| C5 | One research loop per scheme that decides all of a family's members together. Evidence: `eval:h01` and `eval:h04` ran PMSBY and PMJJBY loops separately for each of 3–4 members. | [`2ebc2d4`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/2ebc2d48de468418902c45bdb7f82826cc48ce35) |
| C6 | Low Sonnet effort when it only has to apply fully confirmed cached rules | [`fb5d8f0`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/fb5d8f0a89bb837cc0735b39cd30778d06421995) |
| C7 | Report usage and cost per model | [`3b0ec4c`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/3b0ec4cb3baaa6927e54287c01e7277afd5e16dd) |

The baseline results are in [`52fbe91`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/52fbe910c6e9f955cdfec25a8a5a588bf5b71f45)
and the after results are in [`5faa21b`](https://github.com/rohitraj2496-source/Hackathon_1/commit/5faa21b80b556584c0ff75e33bd81aa31445e22c).

## 5. Caveats

## 1. Before vs after

These are the **9 households that had a wrong or missed scheme in the baseline**: h01–h07, h09 and h10. h08 was
fully correct in the baseline and was not re-run. The "after" column uses the warm-cache h09 run and the batch of
8. Rupee amounts use an assumed rate of ₹88 per US dollar.

| Metric | Baseline | After |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy (TP / (TP + FP + FN)) | 0.50 | **0.86** |
| Precision | 0.71 | **0.97** |
| Recall | 0.64 | **0.89** |
| Wrong schemes (FP) | 8 | **1** |
| Missed schemes (FN) | 10 | **3** |
| Cost per household | $0.93 (≈ ₹82) | **$0.22 (≈ ₹20)** |
| Total cost for 9 households | $8.35 (≈ ₹735) | **$2.00 (≈ ₹176)** |
| Time per household | 147 s | **59 s** |

Per household:

| Household | Baseline: wrong / missed | After: wrong / missed | After: cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| h01 | nfsa_ration, up_shadi_anudan / up_scholarship | — / — | $0.270 |
| h02 | up_shadi_anudan / up_widow_pension, pmjay, pmay_g | — / — | $0.239 |
| h03 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.073 |
| h04 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.185 |
| h05 | — / up_bocw, nfsa_ration | pm_vishwakarma / up_bocw, pmuy | $0.205 |
| h06 | nfsa_ration / up_scholarship | — / up_kanya_sumangala | $0.337 |
| h07 | — / nfsa_ration, pmay_g | — / — | $0.353 |
| h09 | nfsa_ration / — | — / — | $0.112 |
| h10 | nfsa_ration / up_scholarship | — / — | $0.226 |

I've added `EVIDENCE.md` to the repo and pushed it (commit `bd31408`), but it doesn't contain the neatlogs trace IDs you asked for. Haq never saved those IDs when the runs happened, so I have no way to look them up now.

Instead, each bug points to its trace by name, span and session, which is enough to find it in the neatlogs dashboard. For example, the ration-card bug is trace `eval:h03`, span `research:nfsa_ration:household`, session `eee3110444`. The file lists the session IDs for the baseline run, for the aborted re-run that showed the crash and hang bugs, and for the manual test household.

The file contains:
- **Before vs after** for the 9 baseline-error households, overall and per household:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Accuracy | 0.50 | 0.86 |
  | Precision | 0.71 | 0.97 |
  | Recall | 0.64 | 0.89 |
  | Wrong schemes | 8 | 1 |
  | Missed schemes | 10 | 3 |
  | Cost per household | $0.93 (≈₹82) | $0.22 (≈₹20) |
  | Time per household | 147s | 59s |
- **Warm vs cold cache for h09:** $0.112 and 47s warm, $0.241 and 122s cold. It includes the calls, cost and cache reads/writes for each model, which shows that Haiku's structured outputs and prompt caching work.
- **Likely eligible vs confirmed:**
  - 15 likely: 13 expected answers, 2 optional extras, 0 wrong.
  - 44 confirmed: 15 expected answers, 28 optional extras (mostly insurance and pension products), 1 wrong.
  - Counting only confirmed schemes, accuracy is 0.52, precision 0.94 and recall 0.54.
- **Every fix with a GitHub commit link and its evidence:** the 7 accuracy fixes and the resume fix, then the 7 cost changes, each tied to the baseline token numbers.
- **Caveats:** the expected answers still haven't been checked by a person, h08 and h11–h20 haven't been run on the new code, the ₹88/USD rate is assumed, and the h09 runs used 1 worker instead of 4.

While writing the file I caught an error in what I told you last time: there are 44 confirmed predictions, not 15. The overall scores were already correct; only that row was wrong.

To get real trace IDs into future results files, I can have `run_evals.py` save the ID of each household's trace. That's a small change.

def run_one(household: dict) -> dict:
    hid = state.new_household(household["profile"], source=f"eval:{household['id']}")
    t0 = time.time()
    err = None
    try:
        with neatlogs.trace(f"eval:{household['id']}", kind="WORKFLOW", session_id=hid, eval_case=household["id"]):
            run = agent.run(hid)
    except Exception as e:  # keep scoring the rest; a crash counts as predicting nothing
        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        run = state.latest_run(hid)
    elapsed = time.time() - t0
    cards = (run or {}).get("result", {}) or {}
    cards = cards.get("cards", [])
    predicted = {catalog.canonical_id(c["scheme_id"]) for c in cards}
    confirmed = {catalog.canonical_id(c["scheme_id"]) for c in cards if c.get("verification", "confirmed") == "confirmed"}
    research = (run or {}).get("research", {})
    return {
        "id": household["id"], "description": household["description"], "household_state_id": hid,
        "error": err, "seconds": round(elapsed, 1), "cost_usd": (run or {}).get("usage", {}).get("cost_usd", 0.0),
        "usage": (run or {}).get("usage"),
        "predicted": sorted(predicted),
        "expected": [item.get("any_of") or [item["scheme_id"]] for item in household["expected"]],
        "predicted_likely": sorted(predicted - confirmed),
        "score": score(household, predicted),
        "score_confirmed_only": score(household, confirmed),
        "total_missing_inr_per_year": ((run or {}).get("result") or {}).get("total_missing_inr_per_year"),
        "verified_sources": {c["scheme_id"]: c["official_url"] for c in cards},
        "likely_unconfirmed_rules": {c["scheme_id"]: c.get("unconfirmed_rules", []) for c in cards

    data = json.load(open(FAMILIES, encoding="utf-8"))
    households = data["households"]
    if args.only:
        keep = set(args.only.split(","))
        households = [h for h in households if h["id"] in keep]

    previous = sorted(glob.glob("evals/results-*.json"))
    rows = []
    print(f"Running Haq on {len(households)} households (verify={config.VERIFY_MODEL}, fast={config.FAST_MODEL}, effort={config.EFFORT}, "
          f"simulate_failure={config.SIMULATE_FAILURE})\n")
    with neatlogs.trace("eval_suite", kind="WORKFLOW", households=len(households)):
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
            futs = [pool.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, run_one, h) for h in households]
            for fut in as_completed(futs):
                r = fut.result()
                rows.append(r)
                s = r["score"]
                print(f"  {r['id']}: tp={s['tp']} fp={s['fp']} fn={s['fn']}  {r['seconds']:>6.1f}s  ${r['cost_usd']:.3f}"
                      + (f"  ERROR {r['error']}" if r["error"] else "")
                      + (f"  missed={s['missed']}" if s["missed"] else "")
                      + (f"  fp={s['false_positives']}" if s["false_positives"] else ""))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["id"])
    summary = summarize(rows)
    # Same metrics counting only schemes confirmed end-to-end (likely-eligible cards excluded)
    summary["confirmed_only"] = {k: v for k, v in summarize(rows, "score_confirmed_only").items()
                                 if k in ("tp", "fp", "fn", "precision", "recall", "f1", "accuracy")}

    ts = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    out = {
        "timestamp": ts, "git_commit": _git_commit(),
        "config": {"model": config.VERIFY_MODEL, "fast_model": config.FAST_MODEL, "effort": config.EFFORT, "simulate_failure": config.SIMULATE_FAILURE,
                   "only": args.only},
        "summary": summary, "households": rows,
    }
    path = f"evals/results-{ts}.json"
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    print("\n=== Summary ===")
    for k in ("precision", "recall", "f1", "accuracy", "avg_cost_usd", "total_cost_usd", "avg_seconds",
              "recoveries", "conflicts_logged", "unofficial_claims_logged", "likely_predictions", "errors"):
        print(f"  {k:<18} {summary[k]}")
    print(f"  confirmed_only     {summary['confirmed_only']}")
    if previous:
        prev = json.load(open(previous[-1], encoding="utf-8"))["summary"]
        print(f"\n=== Change vs {previous[-1]} ===")
        for k in ("precision", "recall", "accuracy", "avg_cost_usd", "avg_seconds"):
            print(f"  {k:<18} {prev.get(k)} -> {summary[k]}")
    print(f"\nSaved {path}")
    neatlogs.flush()

content.text:
From now on, every run saves its neatlogs trace and session IDs, both in the eval results files and in the app. The change is committed and pushed as `6eea250`, plus `4151898`, which updates `EVIDENCE.md` to link to it. I didn't run any evals or API calls; I tested offline with the model steps stubbed out and neatlogs export turned off.

**What gets saved:**
- **Each trace entry:** the trace ID, the span ID, the span name (e.g. `haq_run`), the workflow and the session ID (the household ID).
- **App runs:** each run keeps a list of trace entries. A resumed run adds one entry per attempt.
- **Interview turns and follow-ups:** the answer message stores the trace entry for that turn.
- **App API:** `GET /api/households/{id}` now returns the session ID and the run's trace entries.
- **Eval results:** each household has a `neatlogs` block with its trace ID, session ID and the run traces inside it. The top of the file has the suite's trace ID.

**One behaviour change in the evals:** before, every household was nested inside a single `eval_suite` trace, so they would all have shared one trace ID. Now each household is its own trace. It's linked back to the suite by a `suite_trace_id` field, which is also saved in the results.

**Checked offline:**
- Every household gets a distinct trace ID, whether households run in parallel or one after another.
- A household's run trace sits inside that household's trace.
- Resuming a run adds a second trace entry.
- The app API returns the trace entries.

The README describes the new fields. `EVIDENCE.md` still says the earlier runs have no trace IDs, because those runs happened before this change. The next eval run will be the first with real trace IDs in its results file.
